quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means no right turns are allowed at this location.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign intersection with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing down to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: When can you park in the striped area next to a disabled parking spot?

options.text: Never.
If you have a disability plate or parking placard.
When all other spaces are full.
If you are only parking for a few minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You can never park in the striped areas next to disabled parking spaces. These spaces are reserved for wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than regular driving.
A bad idea.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes. Defensive drivers stay alert, watch for trouble, have a plan, and know the traffic laws.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of a crash.
It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
It reduces the effects of alcohol.
It has no effect on driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can affect your brain and impair your driving. Mixing alcohol with drugs increases crash risk.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Say no to drinks by saying you are driving.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drinking and driving is to decide before you drink that you will not drive. After drinking, your judgment is impaired, so you may not make safe choices.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: When can you legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane.
Even if you have to drive off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
Anytime.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on multilane roads with two or more lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the pavement to pass.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and carpools.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When you see an accident ahead, you should:

options.text: Focus on your own driving.
Keep driving and do not stop.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Stay focused on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not drive to the scene just to look.

questions.question: A defensive driver should:

options.text: Keep their eyes moving at all times.
Look for problems developing ahead.
Have a plan for what to do if trouble happens.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes. Good defensive drivers stay aware of what is around them, watch for danger, and are ready with a plan if problems occur.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see:

options.text: A flashing red light.
A steady yellow light.
A yellow arrow.
A flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When riding in a car, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back seat.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must always be properly secured in a seat and never standing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must always be properly secured in a seat and never standing.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians cross here. Watch for people entering or crossing the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing train tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning onto train tracks. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots where they cannot see you.
Can stop faster than regular cars.
Need the same amount of space as regular cars to turn.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots where they cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay out of these areas. Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other cars yield first.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a wide intersection and cannot see around other cars. You should:

options.text: Speed up quickly as soon as the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Slowly move your car into each lane as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start turning left until you can see that all the lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: How far a vehicle can stop does NOT depend on:

options.text: How fast you react.
What time of day it is.
How good your brakes are.
What condition your tires are in.

questions.correctAnswerText: What time of day it is.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you react, weather and light conditions, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving ability compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol does.
The same way amphetamines do.
The same way anger does.
The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol does.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol impair your driving in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours affects your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours affects your driving like a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: It is never dangerous.
You react more slowly to hazards.
You usually drive faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down your reaction time to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle that just parked on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked vehicle, assume the driver will open the door as you approach. Use extra caution when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: Is checking your blind spot by turning your head a good driving habit?

options.text: No, it is a bad driving habit.
Yes, it is a good driving habit.
No, it is unnecessary.
No, not if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is a good driving habit.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, always check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals are present. Warning signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or a train's horn. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does a steady red pedestrian hybrid beacon light mean for drivers?

options.text: You may proceed with caution.
You should slow down and get ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
There are no pedestrians nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: Pedestrian hybrid beacons are used at pedestrian crossings. A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: How often must motor vehicles be inspected?

options.text: Once every four years.
Once every three years.
Once every two years.
Once every year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once every year.
questions.explanation: All motor vehicles registered in Texas must be inspected every year at an official inspection station. This includes motorcycles, mopeds, scooters, and autocycles. You must show proof of insurance at the time of inspection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: You are waiting in line at a stop sign. Vehicles ahead pass through with no cross traffic. What must you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always make a complete stop at the stop sign and check for approaching traffic before proceeding. Do not feel pressured by other traffic to skip making a full stop.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any other condition is not ideal. You can be ticketed for speeding even if you are under the posted speed limit if conditions are bad.
